description:
The Rafale M has landed on INS Vikrant, a jet built for an aircraft carrier catapult, on a carrier with a ski-jump ramp. Yet India's first carrier had a steam catapult in 1961, and went to war with it in 1971.
How a catapult throws a fighter in three seconds, how EMALS works, why America is arguing about it, China's Fujian against the USS Ford, and DRDO's electric catapult demonstrator in Pune.
What India still needs before its jets are thrown off an Indian deck.

Some of you will ask, can the Rafale M fly from Vikrant at all? Yes. It was chosen after ramp trials at Goa, and it landed on Vikrant on 29 October. What the ramp costs it is weight at take-off, and the radar aircraft a catapult would carry. How much weight has never been published, so we do not guess.

If that forty thousand crore were your money, what would you build: a ramp, or a catapult?
